One action plan developed 3 land land conflicts successfully resolved by land arbitration committees 77 households receiving livelihoods support (8 men, 53 women, 16 youth) TBD at evaluation - % of targeted returnees and host community households stating an increase in household income. 43 youths (18 women, 25 men) trained in vocational skills such as sewing, designing, welding and tyre repairs from Greida, Ditto, Joghana and Umrakopa. 2 sustainable and eco-friendly area-based plans designed 29% women; 71% men, 33% youth included in the plan development process Two (2) Sudanese Police Force police posts have been constructed in Umrakoba and Joghana villages and equipped with furniture. The 2 posts are operational with a full capacity of police personnel fifteen (15) in each post. A total of 111 Sudanese Police Force officers (6 women, 105 men, inclusive of 60% newly recruited) trained on community-based policing, public safety and security committees and police volunteer schemes, investigation / forensic capacities, case management system. Paralegals, CSO’s and Native administration (40 inclusive of 18 females) were trained on access to justice at Gereida locality. Prosecutors (40 inclusive of 2 women) were trained on roles and responsibilities of their duties, and how to carry out investigations. Prison guards (35 inclusive of 6 women) were trained on SOPs and Human Right Based approaches to prison managements Five (5) community-based resolution mechanisms (CBRMs) were established in Sagor, Umrakopa, Joghana, Ditto and Gereda town and are functioning.
